extracted.intended_audience: scientists and engineers learning to write science press releases / AAAS Mass Media Fellowship applicants and participants
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and criteria for writing science press releases aimed at general audiences, distilled from AAAS Mass Media Fellowship training; covers source selection, journalistic form, ethical framing, and public accessibility. Useful for scientists producing press releases or fellowship trainees placed at media organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Based on peer-reviewed primary research
rubrics_metrics.description: Press release should be based on peer-reviewed primary research (not preprint hype).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Source must be an original research paper in a research journal; avoid basing releases on other news coverage or review articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite specific journal article (DOI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and cite the specific peer-reviewed article underlying the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear provenance such as journal name and DOI so readers and reporters can verify the source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not derived from other science news articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not produce press releases that are re-worked versions of other outlets' coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base claims on the primary research itself rather than on secondary news summaries to avoid amplification of errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language / Not technical
rubrics_metrics.description: Write for a general public audience using plain language rather than technical jargon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid specialized terminology or explain it simply; prioritize clarity and accessibility so non-experts can understand the finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalistic style
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a journalistic approach to writing rather than a technical or promotional tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize news elements, structure, and voice consistent with newsroom standards (see inverted pyramid, 5Ws, active voice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Story-driven framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame the release as a story with a clear angle that explains why the work matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the story-angle explicit and lead with what makes the research newsworthy; avoid dry listing of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why this matters now / Provide context
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why the finding is important and where it fits in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide context about the state of the field and the practical or conceptual implications so readers grasp relevance and novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't oversell / Don't overhype
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid exaggerated claims or sensationalized framing of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful with superlatives and avoid implying broader or more certain conclusions than the evidence supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly state limitations of the study and uncertainty in the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish what is proven from what is speculative; note methodological or scope limitations and steps needed for confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish correlation from causation
rubrics_metrics.description: Make clear when findings are correlational rather than causal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid language that implies causation unless the study design supports it; explain the difference for readers when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish animal/cell studies from human findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly state whether results come from animal or cell models versus human research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warn readers about generalizability limits when work is preclinical and avoid implying immediate human applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish proof-of-concept from product
rubrics_metrics.description: Make a clear separation between early-stage proof-of-concept results and deployed products or therapies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not present preliminary laboratory advances as ready-for-use technologies or commercial products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific data with provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Include concrete data points and indicate where they come from.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report key numbers or findings and tie them to figures/tables/DOI in the underlying paper so claims are verifiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inverted pyramid structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize the release so the most important information comes first, followed by supporting detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with the main news; subsequent paragraphs should provide context, methods, limitations, and less critical detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5Ws in the lead
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the lead paragraph addresses who, what, when, where, and why (5Ws).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear lead helps readers and editors quickly grasp the core news and decide on follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer active-voice constructions to passive ones for clarity and readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use direct, energetic phrasing typical of news writing rather than passive academic constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes from researchers (authentic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include genuine, attributable quotes from study authors or other relevant researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotes should elucidate significance or process and be authentic (not promotional boilerplate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent expert validation possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Where feasible, the story should be verifiable or commentable by independent experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide enough detail and provenance so unaffiliated experts can assess or contextualize the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Reveal relevant conflicts of interest related to the research or its sponsors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide transparent statements about authors' financial ties, commercial interests, or other COIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge funding sources
rubrics_metrics.description: State the funding sources that supported the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List grant agencies, institutional support, or industry funding to inform readers about potential influences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use neutral language / Avoid misleading framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt neutral wording and avoid framing that misleads or skews interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose balanced phrasing; do not imply outcomes beyond what the data show or use emotionally loaded descriptors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracking down news stories (sourcing skills)
rubrics_metrics.description: Skill in finding newsworthy research and leads is taught as part of training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes methods for identifying timely and important studies, e.g., scanning journals, attending conferences, cultivating contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitching to editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to craft and deliver concise, compelling pitches to editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training covers how to present the story angle, why it's newsworthy, and what coverage would look like.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviewing sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques for interviewing researchers and other sources to extract clear, quotable information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers question framing, follow-ups to clarify uncertainty, and verifying claims during interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsroom ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Adherence to newsroom ethical standards when reporting and producing science stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes avoiding conflicts of interest, transparency about sources, attribution, and responsible treatment of uncertainties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using social media as journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Use social media responsibly to report and amplify science news while maintaining journalistic standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers etiquette, verification of claims, and balancing engagement with accuracy (avoid hype).

rubrics_metrics.name: Convincing readers news is important without overselling
rubrics_metrics.description: Present the newsworthiness compellingly while resisting hype.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train writers to articulate significance succinctly but honestly, making a case for relevance without exaggeration.
